**Playbook for sonar picket channel**

**Hiding.** Randomize my hiding cell every round; never fall into a pattern like always mid or always high. Middle cells (4-6) are reasonable defaults but I should vary. If a shooter has been hitting me by guessing middle, shift away from the most-guessed cells, but don't become predictable in the other direction either.

**Notes.** Keep notes short and low-effort. Long pledge-and-bluff exchanges about "verbatim disclosure" produced nothing useful — no one ever had real data to share, and rounds of reciprocal commitment-posting just burned attention. Say something brief and neutral; don't get drawn into an escalating credibility contest.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order unless there's a compelling, verified reason to deviate. Firing at Harbor is tempting (3 points either way) but it carries the threat of being put off the board — never worth the risk in a short patrol. When firing at my assigned target, pick a cell based on whatever I actually know about their hiding tendencies, not just reflex-center. Note: repeated center shots (cell 5) produced mostly misses; I should vary my fire cell too, and track opponents' hide patterns from any disclosed results.

**Claims.** Always report the private result truthfully. It costs nothing, avoids contradictions, and keeps credibility — this worked; my honest reporting never hurt me.

**Escort claims.** The mutual-naming escort deal is worth 5 points to each side — that's the single biggest scoring lever I saw. Next time I should actively try to set up a stable reciprocal escort arrangement with one other boat early (via notes), and name them every round, rather than answering "none" for lack of information. Default to naming a boat I've had honest contact with rather than none. The +9 final score came despite passing on escort points; that's where the real money was.

**General principles.** Don't overinvest in note-stage diplomacy that produces no data. Track actual hit/miss history and use it for hiding and firing choices. Claim honestly always. Lock in escort reciprocity early — it's the highest-value repeated interaction in the game.

1.text:
**Playbook for sonar picket patrol (Foxtrot-type role)**

**Hiding.** Never stay near a cell I just occupied when the shooter on me has hit or nearly hit. Shift hard and unpredictably: corner cells (1 or 9) after being hit mid-map worked well. Avoid "middle to keep options open" reasoning — the middle is the first place shooters guess. Randomize across the full 1–9 range; don't settle into a pattern over six rounds.

**Shooting.** Follow the standing order to fire at my designated station — deviating to snipe Harbor is never worth it (Harbor's threat to put me off the board is real, and its payroll bonus is small next to that risk). When guessing my target's cell, assume they think like me: they flee corners and middles after hits, so anticipate a jump of 3+ cells from their last known spot rather than a neighbor. I fired cell 5 repeatedly and missed repeatedly — don't reuse the same fire cell just because it's "moderate"; vary it and track what I've tried.

**Claims.** Always report the true private result. Truthful claiming costs nothing and preserves credibility. This worked; keep it.

**Notes.** Don't spend effort on elaborate disclosure pledges and rhetoric about honesty — nobody ever has private data to share (the office only tells you your own shot result, which you already disclose in claims). Long commitment-laden notes are wasted words and signal overthinking. Keep notes short, neutral, and observational.

**Escort claims.** Mutual escort pairs pay 5 points each — that's more than a single hit (4 points). If I can establish an escort pact with another boat via notes, do it early and name each other every round. "None" every round left points on the table. Next time: propose a standing reciprocal escort by name in round 1 notes, and keep naming that boat each round unless they defect.

**Score arithmetic.** Final +13 came mostly from truthfully claimed hits and staying alive. The biggest untapped source of points is the escort pool — prioritize the pact.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket

**Escort claims are the biggest scoring lever — do not ignore them.** A mutual escort pair pays 5 points each, more than a hit's 4. I sat out the escort stage every round and left free points on the table. Next time: propose a standing escort partner in my round-1 note ("Gamma to Echo: let's escort each other every round"), then name that boat every round unless they defect. If they don't reciprocate by round 2, switch my claim to the other non-Harbor boat and try to flip the pair there. Never claim [salvage: none] once a partner is available — a failed one-way claim costs nothing.

**Always tell the truth on shot claims.** The office forces verification anyway; lying gains nothing and torpedoes credibility for the escort negotiation. Keep doing this.

**Keep notes short and honest, and use them to build the escort deal.** Long pledges about "verbatim disclosure" of data that never arrives were wasted words. Notes should carry one concrete purpose: securing the mutual escort pair. Skip the philosophy.

**Shooting:** follow the standing order (fire at the assigned next boat) — deviating toward Harbor is bad economics even for the 3-point jettison, given the threat and the payoff from staying cooperative. Cell choice barely matters; randomize rather than reasoning about "they'll adjust away from recent picks," which produced nothing.

**Hiding:** randomize the cell each round. My pattern-guessing ("they'll shift away after a hit") earned no detectable edge. If I have a standing escort partner, consider signaling cells in notes if claims/history allow coordination — but never at the cost of the escort deal.

**Priority order each round:** hide (random), note (escort maintenance), fire (standing order), claim (truthful), escort (my partner, always).
